Scenario
A U.S. bank holding company has filed its Form 10-K.  In Item 5 the registrant discloses information about purchases of its own common equity that occurred during the fourth quarter of 2012.  The narrative explains that during October, November and December the company repurchased shares of common stock and that, for each month, an average price paid per share was calculated.  Elsewhere in the filing the company also presents daily trading-price history, executive-compensation data and many other details that are not directly relevant to the repurchase discussion.

Tools
The following Python functions are available.  Call them when you need specific pieces of information.  (Arguments in square brackets are optional.)

2. get_period_id(month_name: str, year: int = 2012) -> int
   Convert a textual month such as "october" into its unique identifier for that year.

3. get_repurchase_summary(period_id: int) -> Dict
   For the given period identifier, return a dictionary containing:
   • total_shares_purchased
   • avg_price_paid
   • shares_public_program
   • max_shares_remaining

4. get_daily_close_prices(period_id: int) -> List[float]
   Retrieve daily closing prices that were recorded in the database for that month.

5. get_average_prices_for_months(month_names: List[str], year: int = 2012) -> List[float]
   Convenience helper that directly returns the avg_price_paid for each month in the supplied list.

6. compute_range(values: List[float]) -> float
   Given a list of numbers, return max(values) − min(values) rounded to two decimal places.

7. executive_compensation_for(name_substr: str) -> List[Tuple]
   Look up compensation information for executives whose names contain a given substring.

Question
Using the available information, determine the mathematical range (maximum minus minimum) of the average prices paid per share in October, November and December.  Return the result as a number with exactly two decimal places.
